findings.title: Use stored enabled state when deciding login-cache invalidation
findings.body: The original model passed here comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when the associated organization (or organization feature in the realm) is disabled. The cached login query, however, selects IDs using the stored IDP enabled flag, independently of organization enabled state. If a public IDP is cached, its organization is disabled, and the IDP is then changed to hideOnLogin=true or linkOnly=true, both predicates here are false and invalidation is skipped. After the organization is enabled again, getForLogin still returns that IDP, and the login bean's isEnabled() recheck does not exclude hidden or link-only providers. Compare unwrapped persisted models for invalidation so organization state cannot suppress necessary membership changes.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual created provider alias
findings.body: The new test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal alias "alias" instead. The additional callback at line 425 has the same problem. Cleanup therefore requests deletion of a nonexistent provider and leaves the created providers behind, potentially causing cleanup failures and contaminating subsequent tests with enabled realm-level brokers. Capture and use each created provider's actual alias in its cleanup callback.
